## Description

UD Ukrainian-Zhelekhivka is a treebank of a historical regional standard of Ukrainian used in the late 19th and early 20th centuries mostly in the territories that were historically part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. The treebank contains approximately 10,000 tokens from three complete newspaper articles.



UD Ukrainian-Zhelekhivka represents a historical regional variety of Ukrainian written in the Zhelekhivka orthography — a phonetic spelling system first set forth by Yevhen Zhelekhivskyi in his _Malorusko-nimetskyi slovar_ (1886) and revised in 1904 by the Shevchenko Scientific Society in _Ruska pravopys' zi slovarcem_. The orthography was the dominant standard in Galicia and Bukovina, then part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, and remained in use into the 1920s–1930s, by which time these territories had become part of Poland, Romania, and Czechoslovakia respectively.

The texts in this treebank date from the late 19th and early 20th centuries and represent both variants of Zhelekhivka — the original Zhelekhivskyi spelling and the 1904 Shevchenko Scientific Society revision. Zhelekhivka differs from the modern Ukrainian orthographic standard in a number of respects. Notably, it differs in word segmentation: the reflexive clitic ся and the future-tense markers му, меш, ме, мемо, мете, муть most often follow the verb as separate words; particles such as ж, же, б, би are usually, though not always consistently, written together with the preceding word. Other characteristic features include the letter ї in place of historical е and ѣ (лїд, слїдство), the absence of an apostrophe after labial consonants before я, ю, є (пять, звязок), a soft sign marking palatalization of с, з, ц before a following soft consonant (сьвіт, сьвято), and the letter ґ in borrowings (ґенеральний, ґазета); for a fuller list of features and examples, see [1].

[1] Yurii Chemerys, Olesia Nakhlik, Andriy Rysin, Maria Shvedova. Normalization of a Historic Western Ukrainian orthographic system Zhelekhivka in the Ukrainian Language Reference Corpus (GRAC). In Proceedings of the IEEE 18th International Conference on Computer Sciences and Information Technologies (CSIT). 20 Oct. 2023. Lviv, Ukraine. DOI: 10.1109/CSIT61576.2023.10324255.

<h2>Syntax</h2>

<h3>Auxiliary Verbs and Copula</h3>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 1 lemmas as copulas (<a>cop</a>). Examples: бути.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 4 lemmas as auxiliaries (<a>aux</a>). Examples: мати, б, би, бути.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Core Arguments, Oblique Arguments and Adjuncts</h3>

<h3>Reflexive Verbs</h3>

<ul>
  <li>This corpus contains 62 lemmas that occur at least once with an <a>expl:pv</a> child. Examples: здавати ся, перемінити ся, сподівати ся, втручати ся, згодити ся, стати ся, лишати ся, лишити ся, визволити ся, визначати ся, відцурати ся, звати ся, зупинити ся, тлумити ся, бити ся, бороти ся, вдати ся, вернути ся, взяти ся, виховати ся, вступити ся, відважити ся, відрікати ся, з'єднати ся, займати ся, запевнити ся, заходити ся, зберегти ся, здати ся, змагати ся, зупиняти ся, користувати ся, корити ся, лити ся, набирати ся, називати ся, насовувати ся, обмежити ся, обійти ся, організувати ся, переняти ся, питати ся, позбути ся, посоромити ся, поступити ся, починати ся, провинити ся, прокинути ся, піклувати ся, родити ся</li>
</ul>


<h3>Verbs with Reflexive Core Objects</h3>

<ul>
  <li>This corpus contains 11 lemmas that occur at least once with a reflexive core object (<a>obj</a> or <a>iobj</a>). Examples: придбати собі, поставити себе, визволити ся, виправдувати себе, забрати собі, здавати собі, могти собі, поступати собі, почував себе, присвоювати собі, склали собі</li>
    <ul>
      <li>Out of those, 2 lemmas occurred more than once, but never without a reflexive dependent. Examples: придбати, поставити</li>
    </ul>
</ul>

<h3>Relations Overview</h3>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 14 relation subtypes: <a>acl:relcl</a>, <a>advmod:det</a>, <a>advmod:emph</a>, <a>advmod:neg</a>, <a>det:numgov</a>, <a>det:nummod</a>, <a>expl:pv</a>, <a>flat:foreign</a>, <a>flat:name</a>, <a>nsubj:outer</a>, <a>nsubj:pass</a>, <a>nummod:gov</a>, <a>obl:agent</a>, <a>obl:arg</a></li>
<li>The following 6 relation types are not used in this corpus at all: <a>dislocated</a>, <a>clf</a>, <a>list</a>, <a>goeswith</a>, <a>reparandum</a>, <a>dep</a></li>
</ul>
